MU.thesis: Screen rank 1: HBM memory for AI accelerators, +533pp vs SPY over 12m. PE 14 looks cheap, but low multiples at a memory-cycle peak are the classic trap, and it sits 14% below its June high.

AMD.thesis: Rank 2: new 52-week high on Oct 2 and +37pp vs SPY in September alone. PE 163 means the accelerator ramp has to keep delivering; the hard stop does the risk work, not the valuation.

CRWD.thesis: Rank 3: at a 52-week high, +155pp vs SPY over 6m. Barely profitable on GAAP, so this is a pure growth-and-trend position.

NET.thesis: Rank 4: steady uptrend all year, +48pp vs SPY over 6m. Unprofitable on GAAP and the richest valuation in the book.

ANET.thesis: Rank 5 and the best v1 holding: AI datacenter networking, carried over from the original book.

TSM.thesis: Rank 6: manufactures nearly every AI chip in this book, within 1.3% of its high at PE 34. The most reasonably priced name here.

NVDA.thesis: 7th eligible: AI compute leader within 1.1% of its high. Carried over from v1.

AAPL.thesis: 8th eligible: +15pp vs SPY over 12m and 3.4% below its high. The lowest-beta name and only consumer exposure in the book. Carried over from v1.

holdings_update.objective: Beat SPY via concentrated, equal-weight dual-momentum book; accepts materially higher volatility than the index
